name: IT asset, licence and estate records
one_line: The organizational situation of keeping a maintained record of the IT estate - what hardware and software exist, who holds each item, what it is entitled or licensed to run, and how the estate is wired together. The organizing anchor is the ESTATE as a standing inventory, not any one purchase, which is what separates it from the sourcing event that bought the item and the contract that licenses it. Absorbs the legacy rows soft.it-asset-inventory (ROW) and soft.network-diagram (FOLD) - a diagram describes the same estate the register lists. A PLACEHOLDER TEMPLATE ROW written to J-DEPTH: it recognizes the situation and writes NO field rows, because the business_operations schema declares none.

proposed_fields.example: the entity or internal unit whose estate this register describes
proposed_fields.why_no_existing_key: SECONDING, NOT MINTING. This row proposes no key of its own. It seconds the `organization` proposal already carried by the landed `business_operations` schema row - the same key `construction_property` also seconds, with that row's own instruction that it "should be adjudicated once, there, for both." The argument transfers without change: the fact an estate register needs is CUSTODY - whose estate this is - and `our_firm` (authorship), `client` (counterparty), `institution` (the finance-side holder), `school`, `lab` and `venue` all name other roles. R1c should settle this as ONE canonical-list question across the family, and this row must not be counted as a third competing proposal.
proposed_fields.destination_eligible_why: Seconded as FALSE, and this row's evidence strengthens the schema's reason rather than weakening it. An IT estate corpus is almost always single-entity, so an `organization` level here is the vanity level 00 forbids outright: "A folder should not become a collection point for everything produced by the same person or organization." The user may still add it - "The system recommends an order based on the domain template, but the user can reverse, remove, add, or flatten dimensions."
proposed_fields.reliability_why: Seconded unchanged at `possible`. This row adds one estate-specific reason the ceiling cannot be raised: the entity name most reliably present on an asset register is often the VENDOR's, printed on an export header or a licence certificate, not the custodian's. Reading the strongest entity token would systematically read the wrong role.

proposed_fields.example: the management period a stocktake, licence reconciliation or refresh plan belongs to
proposed_fields.why_no_existing_key: SECONDING, NOT MINTING. Same key, same single adjudication as above; the schema row's argument (an entity's management calendar is not a jurisdiction's `tax_year`, and reusing `tax_year` would quietly assert that it does) is adopted verbatim in substance. This row's own reason for wanting it: a licence reconciliation and a stocktake are period artefacts of a management calendar, and a renewal or true-up date is set by a subscription term rather than by any statutory year.
proposed_fields.destination_eligible_why: Seconded as TRUE and explicitly NOT FIRST, for a reason sharper on this row than on the schema: a register is a LIVING document re-saved rather than a dated series, so a period level placed above the estate would scatter one register's versions across calendar folders. 00: "For document and record domains, project, function, or subject usually comes before time because putting year first scatters related work across calendar folders."
proposed_fields.reliability_why: Seconded unchanged, and this row writes no regex and no term list; R2/R6 own those. This row records one caution for R1c: the date token most common on this row's files is a machine-generated EXPORT date in a filename (`intune_device_export_20260301.csv`), which is a capture timestamp for a snapshot and not a fiscal period at all. A rule family that cannot separate the two must sit at `possible`, not `validated`.

deterministic: PRECONDITION: every entry below is a DETECTION signal, never an extraction licence - this template's schema declares no field rows (PR-6; D1's deferral stands). “Privacy policy must be enforced before content reaches any model or external connector.”

a tabular structure whose header row carries asset-identity columns - asset tag, serial number, hostname, model - together with an assignment or location column naming a person, a team or a site. Identity plus custody in one header is the shape. “Tables matter because resumes, forms, applications, invoices, and administrative documents often place their most useful information in cells rather than body paragraphs.”
an entitlement structure pairing a named software product with a seat or quantity count and a renewal or expiry date, often with an assigned-versus-purchased comparison.
a labelled export from a device-management or directory system: a machine-generated filename, a header row naming operating system, last check-in and enrolled user, and one row per device.
a diagram whose text layer carries estate tokens - subnet or CIDR notation, VLAN identifiers, hostnames, rack or switch labels - rather than the dimensioned geometry of an engineering drawing.
a device-handover or acceptance structure pairing one named individual, one asset identifier and a date of issue or return.
a disposal or secure-destruction certificate structure naming an asset identifier and a destruction method.
needs_llm: PRECONDITION: any model step runs after P7 and under the user's policy, and must abstain rather than guess: “A model that cannot cite sufficient evidence must return unknown.”

separating an IT asset register from a fixed-asset register kept for accounting, a stocktake of goods for sale, a plant and equipment register, or a shipping manifest - all four are the same identity-plus-quantity table with different intent. “Topic answers what a file is about, while purpose answers what the file was for.”
deciding whether a network or system diagram documents an as-built estate (this row) or proposes a design (an engineering or software architecture artifact).
an unlabeled spreadsheet of equipment with no header row, or a free-prose description of the estate written in a handover note.

a purpose-coherent estate packet whose members are individually unremarkable - a register, two diagrams, a licence certificate and a blank handover form. “The documents are content-incoherent but purpose-coherent.”
never_alone: a serial-, MAC- or asset-tag-shaped token alone. Every warranty card, invoice and repair receipt carries one, and none of those is an inventory record - this is the tempting false file for this row.
a spreadsheet alone, or a header row naming quantities alone. A quantity table is the most generic structure in office work.

an extension or a source_type alone - 00: “The engine should treat the file extension as a routing signal rather than an assumption about meaning, inspect the real MIME type or file signature where possible, and dispatch each file to a type-specific extractor.”
a hardware or software vendor's name alone - a vendor appears on an invoice, a marketing PDF and a support email as readily as on a register.

an organisation's name alone, read across by inference from “A university name alone should not create a group because Columbia can appear as an authoring school, course provider, target institution, employer, research venue, or merely a cited organization.”
a diagram file alone: .vsdx, .drawio and .png hold floor plans, org charts and process maps just as often as network topologies.
a bare 4-digit number read as a year, a reference, or a version.

membership in a download session that dropped a whole pack at once - “A session should never be treated as proof of topic, and it should not carry the same confidence as a hash match or a directly extracted document fact.”
an OCR'd photograph of an asset label alone, without a register or handover structure around it.

a licence-key- or product-key-shaped token alone. It appears on retail packaging photographs, in a confirmation email, inside a README and in a screenshot as readily as on an entitlement record - and where it is real it is credential material governed by 00's protected-state sentence, not activation evidence.

a business-function word such as IT, inventory, asset or estate, in a filename or a parent folder. The schema anchor's rule for this family is that function words are VALUES of a function dimension, not evidence; every detection signal must pair a structure with a labelled slot.

work_types: device handover, issue or return form
grouping_reasons: one estate snapshot: the register, its supporting exports and the diagrams generated for the same review date, held together by purpose rather than content. “The documents are content-incoherent but purpose-coherent.”
one register across its versions - the same workbook re-saved quarterly is a version family, not nine domains.

one asset across its life - purchase, handover, repair, disposal - which is a real reason to group and the one most likely to tempt a custodian's name onto a stray receipt. “The graph does not automatically copy those missing facts onto sparse files.”
no group at all is a valid outcome: a single licence certificate with no register nearby is a standalone record.

template.why: Empty by binding contract: business_operations declares no field rows (J-IND / PR-6, D1's deferral as narrowed, _CONTRACT rules 10 and 15), so no dimension can branch - a dimension naming an undeclared field opens a tree level no fact could ever fill. Held as prose for the pass that may license fields: the natural anchor is the organisation or site whose estate this is, then the asset class (end-user device, server, network, software entitlement), then the document function; a snapshot date would sit last because a register is a living document re-saved rather than a dated series. “The recommendation should follow the practical rule that a parent dimension should provide the context required to understand the child.” Not time-first: “For document and record domains, project, function, or subject usually comes before time because putting year first scatters related work across calendar folders.” The user may reverse, remove or flatten any of this later; this is a recommendation, not a frozen filesystem. Privacy caveat that is specific to this row: an asset register is a staff directory joined to a serial-number list, and a network diagram is a map of how to reach the estate, so neither should acquire automatic internal depth. “Protected branches should have configurable redaction in the canvas and review screens”.

collides_with.signal: A fixed-asset register kept for depreciation lists the same machines with the same serials. The discriminating evidence: custody and configuration columns - assigned to, location, OS, warranty cover - support this row; acquisition cost, depreciation method, net book value and a posting reference support the accounting register. Provenance: inference.

Plant and equipment registers share the identity-plus-custody table exactly. The discriminating evidence: hostnames, operating systems, licence entitlements and network addressing support this row; machine numbers, calibration due dates, maintenance intervals and criticality ratings support the plant register. Provenance: inference.

The sourcing event that bought the fleet and the register that lists it name the same models and the same supplier. The discriminating evidence: a solicitation reference, a bid comparison or an award letter is the event; a standing list with custody columns is this row. Provenance: inference.

A software entitlement certificate is simultaneously an inventory line and a contractual instrument, and the renewal date appears in both. The discriminating evidence: an obligations register, notice periods and executed signature blocks support contract administration; a seat count reconciled against assignments supports this row. Provenance: inference.

Device issue and return forms are produced by the joiner and leaver process and filed by both functions. The discriminating evidence: a checklist spanning accounts, payroll, induction and access supports hr; a form anchored on one asset identifier with no employment content supports this row. Provenance: inference.

Site records, floor plans and access-badge lists share the register-and-diagram shape and often the same site name. The discriminating evidence: rooms, desks, keys, maintenance contracts and premises support facilities; hostnames, entitlements and device custody support this row. Provenance: inference.

An architecture or infrastructure diagram committed beside source code describes systems rather than an administered estate. The discriminating evidence: residence in a repository with code and configuration, and service-level rather than device-level naming, supports the software project; an asset tag, a custodian and a purchase or warranty anchor supports this row. Provenance: inference.

An approved-supplier register and an asset register are the same identity-plus-owner table, and the hardware vendor named on the estate export is often the same organisation the supplier file is about. The discriminating evidence: a relationship owner, a diligence questionnaire, an insurance certificate or a scorecard supports vendor-management; a per-DEVICE row carrying a serial, a custodian and a warranty or lifecycle date supports this row. Stated to match that row's own boundary language, which routes its reciprocal-facing procurement and contract signals through this row. Provenance: inference.

A device-management export, a licence certificate and a build sheet routinely carry recovery keys, local administrator passwords, product keys or certificate material in a column nobody looked at. The discriminating evidence: an exact recognized credential format, a key/password export structure or a vault container supports identity, whose protection runs FIRST as a safety domain (CONNECTION section 4 step 5); an estate table whose columns are identity and custody supports this row. Where both are present this is co-activation on disjoint evidence, not a contest, and the stricter side governs the credential span. Provenance: inference.

Asset records are pulled into ticket handling constantly, and a support export lists devices and users in the same shape. The discriminating evidence: a ticket or case identifier, a status/priority/assignee column set and a chronological correspondence thread supports support-operations; a standing register with no case anchor supports this row. The gist pass left this neighbour deliberately unedged, calling the confusion one of lookup rather than of belonging; that was too generous - a support system's device export contests real bytes with a device-management export, and the edge is drawn here. Provenance: inference.

also_holds_with.signal: A signed device handover form is one file under two situations on disjoint evidence - the asset identifier and its custody transfer for this row, the joiner-or-leaver process and the named employee for hr. This is co-activation, not a mutex, and where it happens the hr side governs the individual-identifying members, per the schema row's rule that where one file crosses, the stricter side wins. AUTHORED ONE-WAY HERE: the hr schema is not yet written and R1c owes the reciprocal. Provenance: inference.

An estate export that carries a real credential column holds both an inventory structure and credential material, on genuinely disjoint evidence. identity is a safety domain, so its activation unlocks protection before any model or placement path; this row's activation unlocks nothing beyond a field-less schema. One-way here; R1c owes the reciprocal. Provenance: inference.

falls_through_to.why: The home for a standalone licence certificate, warranty record, handover form or disposal certificate with no register or accepted estate group around it. “Independent Records may live under Personal/Independent Records and hold standalone certificates, notices, confirmations, forms, and PDFs that have a durable purpose but no broader group.”

The cautious outcome for an unlabeled equipment spreadsheet or an ambiguous diagram whose estate meaning is unresolved. “Review Later may hold files whose meaning is partly understood but whose final location requires a future decision.”

The correct home for the purchase side that this row must not absorb - an isolated hardware invoice, order confirmation or subscription receipt. “Receipts and Confirmations may hold isolated invoices, delivery confirmations, booking records, boarding passes, purchase receipts, event tickets, and similar transactional documents.”

The safe outcome for a password-protected estate archive or an unreadable diagram binary. “Unsupported or Encrypted may hold—or, more safely, represent without moving—password-protected archives, unreadable documents, damaged files, and unknown formats.”

The home for a photograph of a device or a label with no accepted inventory association. “One-Off Images may live under Photos/One-Off Images and hold images with no event, project, reference collection, or photo-family association.”

sensitivity_why: An asset register is a staff list joined to a hardware list: it concentrates many named individuals' custody, location and equipment in one file, and an estate diagram is a description of how to reach the systems those people use. 00 names the corpus this product handles - it “can include identity documents, account statements, tax records, medical information, legal records, credentials, private correspondence, GPS metadata, employment materials, and educational records.” - and licence keys and credential-bearing exports fall under “A scanned passport, tax statement, medical document, authentication key, or account record should enter a protected state immediately.”. The operative limits are 00's: “Protected material should not be included in cloud-model prompts by default, should not display raw content in general group summaries, and should not be moved automatically without a user policy that explicitly permits it.”. Two things are stricter here than the family default, and both are stated as this row's own reasons rather than as generic caution. FIRST, the exposed parties are third parties who cannot consent: an asset register is a roster of NAMED EMPLOYEES joined to the equipment each carries and often to where they sit, and none of those people is operating this product. The schema anchor names this property as its privacy leg; on this row it is not an occasional appendix but the register's PRIMARY axis, which is why the posture is stricter than the family default rather than equal to it. SECOND, an estate diagram and a device export are operationally exploitable in a way an ordinary business record is not - a topology is a description of how to reach the systems, and a build sheet or licence record may carry key material. The operative local-only limit is 00's: "Paths, complete extracted text, OCR output, file hashes, image EXIF, GPS, user edits, group memberships, and raw sensitive values should remain local." Concretely, this row recommends that a register or diagram be summarised by STRUCTURE (a device table of N columns; a topology diagram) rather than by contents, that no custodian name and no address token reach a cloud prompt or a general group summary, and that this row never acquire automatic internal depth. This row assigns only the catalogue value potentially_sensitive; it does not assign, alias, rank, or infer a P7 handling class.
open_question: Where the boundary sits for a single person or a household. A freelancer's list of their own laptops, warranties and software subscriptions has exactly this shape and none of the organisational anchor, and it arguably belongs with personal administration rather than with an IT function. The row does not resolve it, because deciding it silently would put someone's personal device list under a work branch. A second question this pass could not settle, and did not smooth: whether the third-party posture argued in sensitivity_why is expressible at all in a catalogue that assigns no P7 handling class. The alternatives are (a) leave it as prose and accept that nothing enforces it, at the cost that the strictest thing about this row is the thing the machine cannot read, or (b) let R1c mint a catalogue-level marker for third-party-personal-data concentration covering this row, hr and the parts of business_operations that carry staff appendices - at the cost of adding vocabulary to a field-less placeholder. This row recommends (b) and refuses to do it unilaterally.
